A die shows an even number in 3 of its 6 faces, so the probability of a success is \(p = \dfrac{3}{6} = \dfrac{1}{2}\) and \(q = \dfrac{1}{2}\), with \(n = 100\).
Hence \(X \sim B\left(100, \dfrac{1}{2}\right)\) and the variance is \(npq = 100 \times \dfrac{1}{2} \times \dfrac{1}{2} = 25\).
\(\therefore\) the standard deviation is \(\sqrt{npq} = \sqrt{25} = 5\).

Here \(np = 4\) and \(npq = 2\), so dividing gives \(q = \dfrac{2}{4} = \dfrac{1}{2}\), hence \(p = \dfrac{1}{2}\) and \(n = \dfrac{4}{p} = 8\).
Therefore \(P(X = 2) = \binom{8}{2}\left(\dfrac{1}{2}\right)^{2}\left(\dfrac{1}{2}\right)^{6} = 28 \times \dfrac{1}{2^{8}}\).
\(\therefore P(X = 2) = \dfrac{28}{256}\).

Here \(p = \dfrac{3}{4}\), \(q = \dfrac{1}{4}\); if he fires \(n\) times then \(P(\text{at least one hit}) = 1 - \left(\dfrac{1}{4}\right)^{n}\).
We need \(1 - \left(\dfrac{1}{4}\right)^{n} > 0.99\), i.e. \(\left(\dfrac{1}{4}\right)^{n} < 0.01\), i.e. \(4^{n} > 100\).
Since \(4^{3} = 64 < 100\) and \(4^{4} = 256 > 100\), the least such \(n\) is \(4\) (indeed \(1 - \dfrac{1}{256} = 0.99609 > 0.99\), while for \(n = 3\), \(1 - \dfrac{1}{64} = 0.98437 < 0.99\)).
\(\therefore n = 4\).

Given \(np = 18\) and \(npq = 12\), dividing gives \(q = \dfrac{12}{18} = \dfrac{2}{3}\), so \(p = 1 - q = \dfrac{1}{3}\).
Then \(n = \dfrac{18}{p} = 18 \times 3\).
\(\therefore n = 54\).
